blocks.content: A Service that seems unreachable almost always traces back to the same root cause covered in the Services module: an empty, or incorrect, Endpoints list, this topic covers the systematic order to check it.
Exactly as covered in the Endpoint topic, the single most common reason a Service seems unreachable is that its Endpoints list is genuinely empty, no Pods currently match its selector at all.

blocks.alt: The exact cause flagged directly in the Services module, still the most common one in practice

blocks.content:
kubectl get endpoints my-app
# NAME     ENDPOINTS
# my-app   <none>

blocks.content: 2. Check: Does the Selector Actually Match
blocks.text: 2. Check: Does the Selector Actually Match

blocks.content: A very common, easy typo, a Service's selector referencing app: myapp while the actual Pods are labeled app: my-app, is enough to produce exactly this empty-Endpoints symptom.

blocks.alt: A single-character typo, enough on its own to cause this exact symptom

blocks.content: 3. Check: Are the Matching Pods Actually Ready
blocks.text: 3. Check: Are the Matching Pods Actually Ready

blocks.content: This connects directly to the Readiness Probe topic, Pods that match the selector but are not currently passing their readiness check are deliberately excluded from Endpoints, they exist, but the Service correctly will not route to them.

blocks.alt: Matching, but deliberately excluded, exactly the readiness mechanism covered earlier

blocks.content: A genuine, common configuration mistake, confusing a Service's exposed port with the actual targetPort the container listens on, results in traffic being routed correctly, to the wrong port entirely.

blocks.alt: A subtle mismatch, traffic routed correctly, but to the wrong port

blocks.content: 5. The Systematic Order to Check These
blocks.text: 5. The Systematic Order to Check These

blocks.content: In practice, check in this order: Endpoints (is anything even matched at all), then Pod readiness (are matches actually eligible), then port configuration (is the traffic aimed at the right port), this order catches the most common issues fastest.

blocks.alt: A deliberate order, catching the most common real issues fastest

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: An unreachable Service almost always traces back to Endpoints, either genuinely empty (selector mismatch) or excluding Pods that are matched but not Ready.
Checking Endpoints, then Pod readiness, then port configuration, in that order, catches the vast majority of real Service reachability issues fastest.
